disclaimer: These labels are research references derived from official-source text in the local corpus. They are not lawyer-prepared labels, legal advice, or independent expert validation.
independenceMethod: The label builder reads only candidate-cases.jsonl, statutes.json, and legal-sources/manifest.json. It does not import, read, or accept blind-predictions.json.
sourcePolicy: Only official Government of India legal publications are accepted.

records.caseText: On 20 June 2024, property was dishonestly moved out of another person's possession without consent.

sources.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
sources.support: Section 378 states the defining elements reflected in the case facts.

sources.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
sources.support: Section 379 supplies the general punishment for theft.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: The repeal-and-savings clause preserves liabilities and proceedings for offences committed under the repealed IPC.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.support: Appoints 1 July 2024 as the commencement date for BNS, except BNS section 106(2).

records.justification: The alleged conduct predates BNS commencement. The stated elements track IPC section 378 directly; section 379 is an acceptable associated punishment provision.

records.caseText: On 12 July 2024, movable property was dishonestly taken from another person's possession without consent.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: Section 303 contains both the definition and general punishment for theft.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.support: Appoints 1 July 2024 as the commencement date for BNS, except BNS section 106(2).

records.justification: The alleged conduct is after BNS commencement, and the stated elements track BNS section 303(1).

records.caseText: The alleged act occurred on 18 June 2024 and intentionally caused another person's death.
factsNeedingReference: circumstances relevant to murder clauses and exceptions

sources.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
sources.support: Section 299 covers causing death with intention to cause death.

sources.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
sources.support: Section 300 distinguishes murder and contains fact-dependent exceptions.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: The repeal-and-savings clause preserves IPC liability for pre-commencement conduct.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.support: Appoints 1 July 2024 as the commencement date for BNS, except BNS section 106(2).

records.justification: The date fixes the IPC framework, but the short facts do not address the circumstances and exceptions needed to choose uniquely between IPC sections 299 and 300.
records.expertReviewReason: A unique homicide provision requires additional facts or expert legal characterization.

records.caseText: On 12 July 2024, a person was deceived and dishonestly induced to deliver property.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: Section 318(1) defines cheating and section 318(4) addresses dishonest inducement to deliver property.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.support: Appoints 1 July 2024 as the commencement date for BNS, except BNS section 106(2).

records.justification: The alleged conduct is after BNS commencement. BNS section 318(1) and (4) directly address deception followed by dishonest inducement to deliver property.

records.caseText: A deceptive course of conduct continued from 20 June 2024 until 12 July 2024 and caused delivery of property.
factsNeedingReference: whether the conduct is legally continuing

acceptable.title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property

sources.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
sources.support: Section 415 defines cheating under IPC.

sources.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
sources.support: Section 420 addresses cheating that dishonestly induces delivery of property.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: Section 318 contains the BNS cheating provisions.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: The repeal-and-savings clause preserves pre-commencement IPC liabilities.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.support: Appoints 1 July 2024 as the commencement date for BNS, except BNS section 106(2).

records.justification: The stated period crosses BNS commencement. Both IPC and BNS cheating provisions are textually relevant, but the authoritative texts alone do not determine offence completion or charging treatment for this fact pattern.
records.expertReviewReason: The cross-commencement treatment and unique Top-1 provision require expert analysis of the alleged continuing conduct.

records.caseText: A complaint alleges dishonest inducement and delivery of property, but does not state when the conduct occurred.
factsNeedingReference: date or period of alleged conduct

sources.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
sources.support: Section 420 is a potentially relevant pre-commencement provision.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: Section 318 is a potentially relevant post-commencement provision.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: The repeal-and-savings clause makes timing material to the governing framework.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.support: Appoints 1 July 2024 as the commencement date for BNS, except BNS section 106(2).

records.justification: The facts omit the date, so the official commencement and savings materials do not permit selection of IPC or BNS. A date clarification is required before ranking a provision.
records.expertReviewReason: The occurrence date is a legally material missing fact.

records.caseText: On 12 July 2024, a crime syndicate carried out continuing unlawful activity involving repeated serious offences.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: Section 111 defines organised crime, organised crime syndicate, and continuing unlawful activity.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.support: Appoints 1 July 2024 as the commencement date for BNS, except BNS section 106(2).

records.justification: The case is post-commencement and expressly invokes an organised crime syndicate and continuing unlawful activity, making BNS section 111 the objective retrieval target. Whether every offence element is proved is outside this retrieval label.

records.caseText: On 12 July 2024, death was allegedly caused by rash and negligent driving and the driver left without reporting the incident.
factsNeedingReference: potentially applicable law outside the corpus

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: Section 106(1) addresses negligent causing of death; section 106(2) text addresses negligent driving followed by failure to report.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.support: Appoints 1 July 2024 as the commencement date for BNS, except BNS section 106(2).

records.justification: The facts track BNS section 106(2), but the official commencement notification expressly excludes that subsection from commencement. The local official-source set does not resolve the resulting charging question or law outside this corpus.
records.expertReviewReason: The specifically matching subsection was not commenced by the available notification; a unique applicable-law and Top-1 answer cannot be assigned from this corpus alone.

records.caseText: On 20 June 2024, repeated unwanted following and electronic monitoring caused fear and distress.

sources.authority: Bureau of Police Research and Development, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
sources.support: The official comparative chart identifies IPC section 354D as stalking and maps it to BNS section 78.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: BNS section 78 provides the corresponding element structure and demonstrates why the omitted facts are material.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: The repeal-and-savings clause preserves IPC liability for pre-commencement conduct.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.support: Appoints 1 July 2024 as the commencement date for BNS, except BNS section 106(2).

records.justification: The date fixes the IPC framework and the official chart identifies IPC section 354D as the stalking provision. However, the case omits facts material to the statutory formulation, and the local corpus lacks primary IPC section 354D text.
records.expertReviewReason: A unique Top-1 label is withheld because material statutory facts and primary IPC section text are unavailable in the approved local source set.

records.caseText: On 12 July 2024, a person was wrongfully prevented from leaving a confined place.
factsNeedingReference: duration or aggravating purpose if any

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Law and Justice
sources.support: Section 127(1) defines wrongful confinement and section 127(2) gives the basic punishment.

sources.authority: Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.support: Appoints 1 July 2024 as the commencement date for BNS, except BNS section 106(2).

records.justification: The alleged conduct is post-commencement and directly tracks the basic wrongful-confinement rule in BNS section 127(1), with section 127(2) as the associated punishment.
